sources: UF/IFAS Extension Manatee County, A Tale of Three Daddy Long Legs: harvestmen (Opiliones) have one fused body, two eyes, no silk and no venom, omnivores; cellar spiders (Pholcidae) have two body parts, eight eyes, silk, and venom considered medically insignificant; crane flies are insects that don't bite or sting; https://blogs.ifas.ufl.edu/manateeco/?p=9645
Penn State Extension, Cellar Spiders: loose irregular webs in dark damp places; vibrate rapidly in the web when disturbed; harmless to people; https://extension.psu.edu/cellar-spiders
UC Riverside, Rick Vetter, The daddy-long-legs myth: no evidence pholcid venom is dangerous to people; the 'fangs too short' claim is false; https://spiders.ucr.edu/daddy-long-legs-myth

Burke Museum, Spider Myths (R. Crawford): cellar spiders are a major predator of other spiders, invading webs; females carry their eggs in their jaws; https://www.burkemuseum.org/collections-and-research/biology/arachnology-and-entomology/spider-myths
MythBusters episode 13 (2004): Adam Savage let a daddy-longlegs (cellar) spider bite him and felt only a brief mild burning sensation.

beats.say: You've heard the daddy long legs has the deadliest venom, and fangs too short to bite you.
But two different animals get that name. And one isn't even a spider.
The harvestman. One round body, two eyes, no silk, and no venom at all.
The cellar spider. Two body parts, eight eyes, and a messy web in your basement.
It does have venom. But there's no evidence it's dangerous to people.
Bother it, and it shakes its web so fast, it blurs.
And the fangs too short story? That's false too.
Subscribe. Part seven is the spider watching you from your window.
